reasons.vendor:
GNS3's own template gives a real explicit vCPU count (1), unlike most
of this batch.
reasons.firmware:
firmware: "uefi" (NPX-1167, rule #59 deviation, live evidence not guessed):
KernelKit's own official x86_64 release qcow2 (github.com/kernelkit/infix
releases) is a real GPT disk with an "EFI System" partition and NO BIOS boot
code at all (confirmed via `fdisk -l` on the raw image) - booted through
netplex's real platform per rule #58, it hung forever at SeaBIOS's "Booting
from Hard Disk..." with the guest pinned near 100% CPU (a real screenshot
confirmed this, not guessed). GNS3's own infix.gns3a doesn't record a firmware
field either way, so this isn't drift from their template - it's this image's
own real, upstream requirement. `ovmf` is already a documented netplex
dependency for exactly this case (docs/DEPENDENCIES.md: "UEFI/Secure-Boot
guests") - qemu.py just never had the loader/nvram wiring to use it until now.
reasons.description: 58): needs UEFI firmware (see firmware=uefi above) - reaches the real Infix/OpenWrt-style login banner on the console. Wave 38.12/NPX-1167.",

settings.description: KernelKit Infix. Real image sourced 2026-09-17 from the project's own official GitHub release (infix-x86_64-v26.08.2.qcow2, github.com/kernelkit/infix) - free/open-source, no vendor account needed. Live-boot-verified through netplex's real platform (rule #58): needs UEFI firmware (see firmware=uefi above) - reaches the real Infix/OpenWrt-style login banner on the console. Wave 38.12/NPX-1167.
